title: Colonoscopy for a child
what: The doctor looks inside your child's large bowel with a thin flexible tube with a camera. For children it is usually done in sleep, under sedation or anesthesia.
why: For blood in the stool, long-lasting diarrhea, belly pain, anemia, poor weight gain, and to monitor inflammatory bowel disease.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 20 to 60 minutes, plus preparation the day before and time to wake up
tell_doctor: All medicines your child takes, and iron supplements
If your child recently had a cold
Whether your child or relatives had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Diet
prepare.text: For 1 to 3 days, food without fiber. Your doctor will give an exact list. The day before, usually only clear liquids.

prepare.title: Cleansing
prepare.text: Your child drinks the cleansing solution as your doctor directs, and the dose depends on weight. To make it easier, it can be chilled and drunk through a straw.

prepare.title: Fasting
prepare.text: Before sedation, your child does not eat or drink for a set time. The clinic will tell you the exact hours.

prepare.title: Talking
prepare.text: Explain in simple words that your child will sleep while the doctor looks at the tummy.

bring: A change of underwear and diapers, if needed
steps: Your child changes clothes and a line is put in a vein, often after a numbing cream
A parent usually stays close while your child falls asleep
Your child sleeps while the doctor gently passes the tube and examines the bowel
If needed, tiny tissue samples are taken for testing
Your child wakes up in a recovery room and you are called in
feel: The procedure itself is not felt during sleep
After waking, there may be sleepiness, fussiness, and a bloated belly
Preparation is the hardest part: frequent loose stools and an unpleasant taste of the solution
after: Eating and drinking are usually allowed once your child is fully awake
Bloating from air goes away in a few hours
Rest at home for the rest of the day
The biopsy result usually comes in 1 to 2 weeks
red_flags: Severe belly pain or a hard belly: call emergency services
Heavy bleeding from the bottom or vomiting blood
Your child is limp, hard to wake, or not drinking

faq.q: My child can't drink all the solution. What should I do?
faq.a: Call the clinic. Sometimes another plan is chosen, but the preparation cannot be skipped.

faq.q: Can I be with my child?
faq.a: Usually a parent stays until your child falls asleep and is there right after waking. Check the rules with the clinic.

reminders.text: Colonoscopy for your child tomorrow. Today only clear liquids, and the solution as your doctor directed. Fasting follows the clinic's times.
